labels.note: Default wait_random() would always return 1s instead of a random value in [0,1].
Default wait_random() range widens to [0,2], changing the documented default behaviour.
Default start of wait_incrementing shifts every wait by 1s; the first wait becomes 1 instead of 0.
Default increment constant; 101 would also be a reasonable setting, so a test only pins the default.
Default floor becomes 1s; with a small multiplier, waits are raised above the correct value.
Wait falls outside [min,max]; min==max raises ZeroDivisionError. This is the core random-wait calculation.
Clamp floor becomes 1, so the default first wait is 1s instead of 0.
multiplier=0 with a finite max reaches math.log(0), which raises ValueError instead of returning min.
